messages:
lena: quick dump of the draft-sampling ablation I ran this morning. focus: speculative/draft pipeline latency vs quality on draft-model-v2.
alex: nice, summary first? numbers pls :eyes:
maya: +1. also include config so we can reproduce.
lena: TL;DR: speculative decoding with a 3B draft (quant q4_0) + 13B verifier (q6_k) gives ~2.6x throughput vs baseline 13B-only at temp=0.2, with a small drop in answer F1 (~1.8 pts) on our QA eval set (n=500). draft-only (no verification) kills quality as expected.
patrick: that throughput is tokens/sec or ms/token?
lena: tokens/sec. baseline 13B-only median 420 tps, spec pipeline 1100 tps. per-token latency median: baseline 2.4ms -> spec 0.95ms (end-to-end avg per token). numbers are on p4d equivalent cluster, batching kept small (batch=4, seq=512 typical).
zhou: how are you counting verification cost? double decode overhead?
lena: verifier still reads proposals but uses a cheap scoring path (logit-check with cache reuse). measured end-to-end latency includes verifier time. verification adds ~18% overhead compared to raw draft generation but overall win because draft is much cheaper.
maya: what's the quality metric precisely?
lena: canonical QA F1 on our inductive set (span-extraction style + normalization). also logged perplexity shift and human-label win-rate (40 prompt pairs annotated by ops for edge cases).
patrick: can you paste the exact config you ran? command + model versions.
lena: sure — here's the gist:
```
# spec run
models:
  draft: "redwood/draft-model-v2-3b-q4_0"
  verifier: "redwood/target-model-13b-q6_k"
speculative:
  draft_tokens_limit: 64
  verify_top_k: 1
  verify_mode: "logit-check"
sampling:
  draft_temp: 0.9
  verifier_temp: 0.2
runtime:
  batch_size: 4
  seq_len: 512
  quant: true
```
alex: draft_temp 0.9 seems high — did you tune it?
lena: yes, high draft temp gives diverse proposals; verifier filters down. we swept draft_temp in [0.2,0.5,0.9,1.2]. best throughput-quality pareto at 0.9. at 1.2 diversity increased but F1 drop >3 pts.
zhou: what about number of proposals? verify_top_k=1 only?
lena: we tried top_k=1/2/3. top_k=1 is best for latency-quality tradeoff. top_k=2 gave tiny F1 gain (0.4 pts) but cost grew ~30%.
maya: did you try quantized verifier vs fp16? any accuracy regression from q6_k?
lena: verifier q6_k had near-identical logits for our eval set (avg KL ~1e-4 relative); human win-rate delta within noise. fp16 verifier slightly better on edge-case hallucinations but latency hit was ~12%.
patrick: model size for draft? only 3B?
lena: tried 1.2B, 3B, 6B. 1.2B was fastest but quality drop >4 pts. 6B matched 3B quality but cost/latency worse. 3B is sweet spot for our workload.
zhou: any interesting failure modes?
lena: yes — long context instruction-following prompts sometimes get broken up by draft proposals causing verifier to prefer shorter completions. mitigated by increasing draft_tokens_limit and enforcing length penalty in verifier scoring.
maya: what about quantization ablation on draft (q4_0 vs q5)?
lena: q4_0 is best perf/quality. q5 slightly better quality (~0.5 F1) but latency worse ~8%. team might choose q5 for narrow-high-quality customers.
patrick: do you have the raw csv with per-prompt diffs? can you drop it in the eval bucket?
lena: uploading now. eval-bot: ingest complete -> /evals/spec-draft/1768123345/raw.csv
eval-bot: summary artifact: /evals/spec-draft/1768123345/summary.json
alex: nice. next steps: run a 2k prompt sweep with more diverse long-form prompts, and a canary on Dedicated to validate tail latencies.
maya: I'll pick up the long-form sweep this week.
lena: thanks — I'll PR the experiment harness and add a README with reproduction steps. filing follow-ups: increase draft_tokens_limit in long prompts, test verifier length-penalty knobs, and run A/B on dedicated pool.
patrick: great, put the PR link here when ready :rocket:
lena: will do. :thumbsup:
